name: Ahijah
overview: Ahijah was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified uniquely as the son of Ehud. His mention in Scripture is brief and primarily genealogical, with no additional notes expanding on his role or actions. This positions him as a figure known chiefly through his lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahijah means '[my] brother is y-h-v-h,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the Lord. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God, but it reveals a connection to divine identity through its meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Ahijah was the son of Ehud, establishing a direct father-son relationship. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ahijah's significance in the biblical narrative rests on his genealogical placement within the tribe of Benjamin as the son of Ehud. While the text does not elaborate on his personal deeds or spiritual contributions, his identification preserves the lineage that is part of God's sovereign plan for His people. His name and tribal affiliation situate him within the covenant community from which Christ ultimately came.
